name: Orangism
summary: Orangism in the Kingdom of the Netherlands is royalism supporting the House of Orange as the country's ruling dynasty. From the 1860s the dominant liberal faction adopted it as a national, apolitical stance that could unite Protestants and Catholics and push aside socialist and denominational politics. It is a symbol-and-loyalty current rather than a full programme, so its economic and social positions are largely undocumented.
scope: The Dutch Orangism of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (restoration of 1813 onward, with its liberal-monarchist form from the 1860s), based on the 1814 constitution, Van Hogendorp's moderate Orangism and te Velde and Petterson's account of nation building. It excludes the pre-1795 pro-stadtholder party of the Dutch Republic, Belgian and Luxembourg Orangism, Northern Irish Orangeism, and the Oranjegekte sports fever. Most positions beyond monarchy, national unity, constitutional rule and class cooperation are low-confidence inferences from its liberal-royalist character.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Liberal Orangism was about national unity rather than wage policy, and a liberal-monarchist would split between market wages and social protection.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Liberal Orangism came from the dominant liberal faction, whose general lean was toward markets, though the sources give no economic programme.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The movement defines no tax position; liberals of the era favoured moderate rates but a unity-focused royalism would avoid class-targeted measures.

cut-welfare.rationale: A movement meant to reconcile social groups would not push welfare cuts, but no document states a welfare position.

worker-ownership.rationale: Orangism's aim of sidelining socialist politics points away from collective worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Nothing in Orangism concerns surveillance; liberal royalists would be split between security and liberty.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The movement never touched drug policy and liberal royalists would be divided.

strong-leader.rationale: The 1814 constitution's drafter Van Hogendorp insisted on constitutional rather than personal rule, and Orangism offers the monarch as a symbol, not a bypass of parliament.

state-harmful.rationale: Orangism is loyalty to a state headed by the House of Orange, so it cannot treat the state as unnecessary.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No documented position; liberals and Protestant monarchists differ.

decide-locally.rationale: The Orange restoration produced a centralised monarchy under the 1814 constitution and Orangism stresses national unity over local particularism.

traditional-family.rationale: Royalism stresses the royal family as a national symbol, but adherents range from Protestant traditionalists to liberals.

more-religion-public.rationale: Liberal Orangism sidelined denominational politics in favour of an apolitical national stance.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Orangism has no theory of gender; adherents would be mixed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Te Velde and Petterson describe Orangism as nation building, with cultural nation building hard to imagine without the monarchy.

gradual-change.rationale: Moderate Orangists such as Van Hogendorp backed ordered constitutional continuity under the dynasty over revolution.

free-trade.rationale: Van Hogendorp, a moderate Orangist, favoured open markets, and the liberals who adopted Orangism leaned the same way, though it is not a core tenet.

open-borders.rationale: A nation-building movement would not endorse open borders, though it never discusses them.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The movement has no stance on climate and adherents would vary.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No documented position; nineteenth-century liberals were optimistic but the movement is not about progress.

revolution-justified.rationale: Orangists were counter-revolutionary in 1813 and Van Hogendorp opposed the Patriots' revolutionary programme, so revolution is rejected.

experts-over-public.rationale: No documented position; liberal elites and populist Orangists of earlier eras differ.

socialized-markets.rationale: Collective ownership of firms belongs to the socialist politics that Orangism was meant to sideline.

basic-income.rationale: The movement has no social-policy programme.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Liberal adherents like Van Hogendorp opposed William I's protectionism, while others accepted it; no unified line exists.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Liberal-led Orangism leans against state direction of investment, but nothing is documented.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing wages is a socialist goal, and Orangism aimed to marginalise socialist politics.

one-party-rule.rationale: The 1814 constitution gave a representative States-General, and Orangism presented itself as an apolitical stance above parties, not a rule of one.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Orangism in the Kingdom of the Netherlands is defined as royalism supporting the House of Orange providing the country's kings and queens.

democracy-best.rationale: Liberal Orangism accepted parliamentary government, but the sources do not tie it to democracy as the best form regardless of outcome.

direct-votes.rationale: Liberal royalism worked through representative institutions rather than referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils replacing parliaments are a socialist form that Orangism was designed to sideline.

right-to-secede.rationale: Orangism was a unifying national stance and the kingdom lost Belgium in 1830, so a secession right would cut against its national-unity aim.

natural-rulers.rationale: Orangists give a dynasty a special role but not a theory of inborn fitness to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Orangist history includes the 1672 lynching of the de Witts and popular 1747 revolt, so adherents would not agree on a flat ban.

separate-church-state.rationale: Liberal Orangism sidelined denominational politics, but the 1814 constitution itself made the Reformed religion the sovereign's.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Liberal Orangism sidelined denominational politics, leaving scripture-based law outside its programme.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The 1814 constitution gave the sovereign command of army and war powers, and Orangism is loyalty to a state, not privatised security.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Orangism united Protestants and Catholics under one national symbol rather than defining the nation by ethnic group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Te Velde and Petterson describe Orangism as bridging classes and religions, opposing the idea of conflict as the driver.

colonial-reparations.rationale: A royalist nation-building movement tied to a former colonial power would lean against reparations, but this is undocumented.

civilizational-union.rationale: Orangism is tied to a single national dynasty, not unions of nations by civilization.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The movement has no environmental philosophy.

limit-population.rationale: No documented position; liberal royalists lean against coercive population policy.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Orangism centres on a personal monarch and constitutional institutions, not algorithmic rule.

restore-past-order.rationale: Orangism served modern nation building and liberal politics rather than undoing the present for a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Orangism presented itself as apolitical but takes no position on pragmatism versus ideology.

direct-action.rationale: An apolitical national stance supporting the established monarchy rejects direct action against parliaments.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Orangism promoted class cooperation and liberal commerce, so it rejects the claim that profit is exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Socialist politics were what liberal Orangism sought to sideline, and a monarchist rejects class dictatorship.

taxation-theft.rationale: The 1814 constitution gives sovereign and States-General authority to levy taxes, a legitimate state power; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Orangism favours national belonging and representative institutions over exit; undocumented.

state-as-business.rationale: A loyalty-to-the-nation movement does not treat citizens as customers; undocumented.

organic-representation.rationale: The 1814 constitution had provincial-estates selection but Orangism endorsed parliament and parties not corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: The 1814 constitution guaranteed religious freedom and Orangism's apolitical stance does not mean state control of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Orangism celebrated existing continuity under the dynasty rather than radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nothing in Orangism seeks expansion; the kingdom lost Belgium in 1830.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Orangism is loyalty to a dynasty within constitutional institutions, not feudal personal oaths.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: A liberal royalism assumes common truth; undocumented.

single-common-good.rationale: Liberal Orangism's national-unity aim treated the nation as one community above sectional politics.

workplace-democracy.rationale: A liberal royalism sidelining socialist politics would not favour democratic company control.

school-vouchers.rationale: Dutch education funding was a denominational issue that Orangism tried to defuse, so no unified line.

national-self-determination.rationale: Orangism supports a Dutch national state under its own dynasty, though it never states a universal principle.

class-collaboration.rationale: Te Velde and Petterson describe Orangism as bridging social and religious divisions, with classes interacting in nation building.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: A movement built on the House of Orange and national heritage would not sacrifice cultural institutions.

workers-nation.rationale: Orangism sought to attach workers to the nation through the monarchy rather than a class international.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The 1814 constitution guarantees equal civil rights across religions and Orangism had no racial doctrine.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Orangism presents the monarchy and state as national and above class, opposing a ruling-class view of the state.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Orangism defends established national institutions; undocumented otherwise.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The 1814 constitution lists education as a state task, so a minimal state is not the Orangist order.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1814 constitution gave equal civil rights to all religions, supporting equality before the law; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The 1814 constitution drew on French-period unified law and Orangism favoured national unity above denominational differences.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The 1814 constitution protected religious freedom for all religions; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion in schools was the central Dutch denominational dispute, and Orangism sought to sidestep it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Liberal Orangism in the constitutional era rested on popular attachment to the House of Orange.

population-transfer.rationale: Orangism's civic unity and the equal rights of the 1814 constitution oppose expelling minorities.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Orangists spoke the republican-liberty vocabulary but the sources give no stance on this formulation.

separated-powers.rationale: Orangist writers tried to adopt Montesquieu's separation of powers before the Patriots took it up, and Van Hogendorp wanted limited monarchy.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Orangism worked to hold a socially and religiously divided nation together under a symbol, rejecting the claim that diversity prevents it.

party-controls-media.rationale: An apolitical liberal royalism has no place for party control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: The 1814 constitution placed the army under the sovereign, not a party; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A socialist measure at odds with liberal royalism, but undocumented.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Orangism claimed to stand above parties and the 1814 constitution had members vote without instructions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The 1814 text gave the sovereign command of army and navy and ministers, while modern Orangism accepts a ceremonial role, so there is no unified line.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The 1814 constitution tied the sovereign to the Reformed Church, which is not episcopal; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

clerical-rule.rationale: Liberal Orangism sidelined denominational politics and has no clerical authority.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Orangism's constitutional-monarchy outlook is cautious about executive tenure, undocumented.

recall-officials.rationale: Representative liberal institutions with members voting without instruction (1814) rather than recall.

people-in-arms.rationale: The 1814 constitution kept command of a regular army with the sovereign.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Orangist history includes farmers among its supporters, but a modern liberal-monarchist movement holds no view on rural versus urban morality.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The restoration of 1813-15 reunited the Low Countries but Orangism today has no stated reunification aim.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Liberal adherents oppose it, though Protestant adherents may differ; undocumented.

minority-language-support.rationale: Orangism's national-unity aim could cut either way on minority languages, and the sources never raise the point.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberal Orangism does not endorse authoritarian development.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Orangism is defined as supporting the House of Orange providing the monarchs, i.e. hereditary rather than elected head of state.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The 1814 constitution protected churches and the Reformed Church was state funded, so curbing them is not the Orangist order.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Liberal Orangism presented loyalty to the House of Orange as a national, apolitical rallying point above party and denominational divisions, though the stub describes this as a presentation by partisan liberals rather than a stated doctrine.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: William I's government did try to hold Belgium, but modern Orangism is not defined by this.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Orangism favours national unity under one dynasty, but the sources give no view on autonomous regions joining a larger state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Orangism is a constitutional royalism with no doctrine of divine descent.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Van Hogendorp insisted William I govern as a constitutional rather than absolute monarch, and Orangism never claimed absolute sovereignty for the princes.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is outside any documented concern of a royalist loyalty movement.

leader-cult.rationale: Orangism honours the royal house as unifying symbol, but not a leader personality cult.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy is outside the movement's documented concerns, and adherents from Protestant and liberal backgrounds would differ.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine alien to Orangism.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Orangism's civic unity does not claim territory on ethnic grounds.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The 1814 constitution protected religious freedom and equal protection of religions.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Orangism concerns a single Dutch national state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Orangism reflects a view of history shaped by dynasty, nation and identity, opposite to Marxist materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is outside the documented concerns of Orangism, and liberals of the period varied on it.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism accepts institutional limits; undocumented.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for public bodies are outside the movement's documented concerns, and adherents would differ.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: A liberal commerce-friendly royalism rejects autarky.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Orangists opposed the Patriots' revolutionary programme and sought order.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Orangism supports a hereditary dynasty; titles and privileges tied to it are not what it opposes.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Dutch royalists of the colonial era held both paternalist and reformist views, and the sources do not settle it.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The movement never touched on this American-style issue.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The liberal and commercial forces that fostered Orangism assumed the existing economy could manage its crises, but the sources give no direct statement.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: A royalist tradition of a former colonial power would not endorse voiding treaties, though undocumented.

elective-rulers.rationale: Orangism is defined as support for the House of Orange providing the kings and queens, which excludes electing the ruler.

minority-veto.rationale: The 1814 constitution had the States-General vote by majority without instructions, with no individual veto; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Orangists backed the stadtholder against the regents but never held a doctrine allowing subjects to depose a monarch, so adherents would not agree.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Liberal Orangism of the 1860s accepted parliamentary government with a symbolic monarch, though the earlier 1814 order gave the prince far more power.

animal-use-humane.rationale: A mainstream liberal royalist holds this middle view, though undocumented.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Orangist history includes nobles and soldiers loyal to the stadtholder and a royal house that stresses public duty and charity.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Orangism mobilised the public in national life around the monarchy, which runs against withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Orangism itself used popular celebrations and royal ritual to bind classes, and its adherents would not call that pacification.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns communist parties, outside Orangism's concerns.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The kingdom lost Belgium in 1830, but no modern Orangism demands its return.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: A civic-national royalism would not give descent-based political leadership, though the sources are silent.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: A movement built on dynastic heritage tends to preserve national monuments, though undocumented on this question.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The 1814 constitution kept the army under the sovereign, but a liberal royalism would not give it a political guardian role.

filial-duty.rationale: Mainstream conservative-liberal royalists value family duty, though undocumented.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Protestant and liberal adherents differ and the sources are silent.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The 1814 constitution had members vote without instructions from electors, the opposite of binding recall; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The 1814 constitution required the States-General to approve the annual budget and Orangism accepted it.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: A commerce-friendly liberal royalism would not generally bar foreign ownership.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A liberal royalism would judge discrimination by intent and law, though undocumented.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: No documented position; a status-quo monarchy prefers stability.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: A liberal royalism would not generally curb funding, though undocumented.

residents-only-property.rationale: A liberal national-unity movement would not favour local purchase restrictions.

job-guarantee.rationale: A liberal royalism sidelining socialist politics leans against state employer-of-last-resort schemes.

democratic-peace.rationale: A liberal royalism would be open to this doctrine, but nothing is documented.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Orangism's loyalty to institutions and national unity rejects general disobedience.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy view conflicts with Orangism's aim of uniting Protestants and Catholics.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: A royal house built on dynastic marriage, with marriage approved by the States-General, cannot treat marriage as a non-legal matter.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Mainstream liberal royalists accept openness, though nothing is documented.

religious-nation.rationale: Liberal Orangism won support from Protestants and Catholics alike by being apolitical about confession.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not an Orangist doctrine; the movement concerns a national monarchy.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Orangism favours national unity over regional claims.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Property respect is compatible with a liberal royalism, though undocumented.

defeat-communism.rationale: Orangism sidelined socialist politics domestically but nothing addresses foreign confrontation.

religion-illusion.rationale: Liberal Orangism won Protestant and Catholic support, and this is a Marxist claim it opposes.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: A socialist-feminist claim outside liberal royalism.

socialized-care.rationale: A liberal royalism sidelining socialist politics would not socialise housework.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settling a majority group to dilute minorities contradicts Orangism's cross-denominational unity project.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Protestant adherents may differ, but liberal Orangism sidelined confessional politics.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The 1814 States-General and later parliament were part of the Orangist order; the apolitical stance aimed to unify, not suppress.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The 1814 constitution gave equal protection to all religions and allowed public worship; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Dutch colonial economy was run that way historically, but Orangism has no stated line.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Orangism defends established royal rule and does not endorse overthrowing rulers on religious grounds.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A critical-theory claim that mainstream Orangism does not hold, though undocumented.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Liberal Orangism presented itself as a national apolitical stance above political divisions.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Orangism sought to include Protestants and Catholics, and a civic monarchy would not define a religion as incompatible, though undocumented regarding Islam.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The 1814 constitution grounded sovereignty in the House of Orange and the States-General represented the people; no divine claim is stated.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The 1814 constitution assigned army and navy command to the sovereign and Orangism rests on the state; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Article 1 and 3 of the 1814 constitution vest sovereignty in the Prince of Orange-Nassau and his legitimate heirs by primogeniture, which is the core of Orangist royalism.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: A mutualist proposal outside the liberal commercial royalism Orangism represents.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A Marxist critique of liberal freedoms that Orangism's liberal base would not share.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The 1814 constitution included provisions on law and criminal procedure and Van Hogendorp insisted on constitutional rule rather than personal decrees.

racial-franchise.rationale: The 1814 constitution defined representation by citizenship and age, not race; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The 1814 constitution gave equal civil rights to all religions; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Orangism aimed to unite Protestants and Catholics, and boycotts of a religious minority contradict that.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Protestant and liberal adherents differ and sources are silent.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The 1814 constitution funded the Reformed Church and protected all faiths, and Orangism won religious support.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Orangism sought to bridge religious divisions through a shared national symbol, in the spirit of accommodation among communities.

vote-delegation.rationale: The 1814 text had members vote without instructions from electors.

rent-control.rationale: A liberal-commercial royalism leans against it, though the sources are silent.

abolish-ip.rationale: A liberal commercial outlook favours property protections.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Orangism mobilised the public through civic celebration but not drilled national-service youth.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The 1814 constitution gave the sovereign command of army and war powers, so pure pacifism is outside the Orangist state; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Te Velde and Petterson trace popular attachment to the House of Orange back before 1813, which stresses continuity.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Liberal Orangism was designed as an apolitical stance and sidelined denominational politics.

culture-before-state.rationale: Orangism built the state under the House of Orange in 1813 and then used the monarchy for cultural nation building.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Orangism united groups and a commerce-friendly liberal base would not restrict the economy to a majority.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A socialist test of socialism that Orangism does not share.

person-over-state.rationale: The 1814 constitution protected religious freedom and rights, and a liberal royalist accepts the individual's dignity, though undocumented.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The 1814 constitution created a centralised monarchy and provincial powers rested on the national order.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Orangism's civic unity across Protestants and Catholics rejects organising by race.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Orangism is defined by loyalty to the House of Orange, and the page lists Belgian and Luxembourg Orangists who backed unions with the Netherlands across language lines.

communal-electorates.rationale: Orangism fought denominational politics in the name of national unity.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: No documented position, and the plot-narrative is unlike Orangism's confident unity project.

capital-controls.rationale: A liberal commercial outlook leans against them.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The sovereign commands the army under the 1814 constitution and Orangism is a loyalist state-supporting stance; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: A liberal commercial outlook does not seek this.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: No documented position, and a unity-focused national project would not endorse local economic experiments.

internal-colonialism.rationale: A leftist framing foreign to Orangism.

farm-price-support.rationale: No documented position; Orangist history includes farmers as supporters (Dutch Republic), but not policy.

workers-own-party.rationale: Orangism sought to sideline socialist politics and bind workers to a national symbol.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The 1814 constitution gave lawmaking to sovereign and States-General, not customary chiefs; reading that clause as an Orangist position on this question is an inference.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: A nation-building movement tends to expect language learning, though undocumented.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1814 constitution gave all existing religions equal protection and civil rights.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: A liberal royalism leans against it, though undocumented.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Liberal Orangism sidelined confessional politics, though Protestant adherents differ.

indirect-election.rationale: The 1814 States-General was chosen by provincial estates, but Orangism accepted broader elections later.

national-church-status.rationale: The 1814 constitution tied the sovereign to the Reformed Church, yet Orangism won Catholic support by being apolitical on denomination, so adherents do not agree.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Orangism sought national unity over regional autonomy for minorities.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Liberal Orangism was used to rally Protestants and Catholics around the monarchy and sideline confessional and socialist parties, which makes opposing denominational politics its point.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Its national, class-cooperating stance joined love of country with social unity across classes, though workers are not its explicit focus.

material-over-identity.rationale: Orangism took no side on the left's strategy; it sought to sideline socialist politics entirely, so the question does not apply cleanly.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The liberal Orangists adopted the cause partly to push aside socialist politics, so a communist-led socialist system is contrary to its position.

missingStatements.text: Politics should not be organised along religious denominations.
missingStatements.rationale: Liberal Orangism was presented as a national apolitical stance meant to sideline denominational and socialist politics in the name of unity.

notes: The Kingdom-era Orangism article is a short stub resting on one source, so positions beyond monarchy, nation building and class and religious unity are inferences. The 1814 constitution is a restoration-era document, whereas liberal Orangism dates from the 1860s; the profile is of the mainstream constitutional-monarchist form.
